back: Drift: the rate a clock gains or loses time. Skew: the difference between two clocks at one instant. Drift causes skew.

front: Worst-case error at 200 ppm after 30 s without sync?
back: 200 × 10⁻⁶ × 30 s = 6 ms. After a day: about 17 s.
Wall clock: date and time, can jump backwards. Monotonic: only moves forward, use it for durations, timeouts and leases on one machine.
It assumes symmetric network paths. Asymmetric delay causes an error of half the asymmetry, undetectable from one exchange.
Slew: run slightly fast or slow to correct small offsets (stays monotonic). Step: jump the clock, possibly backwards, for large offsets.
Same process and a first; or a is a send and b its receive; or transitively through other events. Otherwise a and b are concurrent.
Increment before each event or send. On receive: counter = max(counter, received) + 1.
a → b implies L(a) is lower than L(b). The converse does not hold: lower timestamps may be concurrent.

front: How to get a total order from Lamport clocks?
back: Order by (counter, process ID). Consistent with causality and identical on every node.
Increment your own entry on each event. On receive: element-wise max with the incoming vector, then increment your own entry.

front: When are two vector clocks concurrent?
back: When neither is ≤ the other in every entry, e.g. [2,1,0] vs [1,1,1].
One entry per participant, so they grow with writers. Dynamo truncated old entries; Riak moved to dotted version vectors.

front: How does LWW lose the newer write?
back: A server with a fast clock stamps an older write with a later time, so it beats genuinely newer writes. Silently.

front: Three ways to handle concurrent writes without LWW?
back: Keep siblings via version vectors and merge on read; use CRDTs; route each key's writes through one owner.
Physical time plus a logical counter: stays near wall-clock time, never goes backwards, respects causality. Used by CockroachDB.
TT.now() returns an interval of uncertainty ε. Spanner waits until the commit timestamp is surely past (about 2ε) before exposing a commit.
